Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Age: 22 years
Sex: [redacted]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Ordering Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL HISTORY
This 22-year-old patient presents with a slow-growing mass in the knee region. Clinical and radiological findings raise suspicion for synovial sarcoma. No relevant family history reported.

REASON FOR REFERRAL
Molecular confirmation of suspected synovial sarcoma

SPECIMEN TYPE
Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue from knee mass biopsy

TEST PERFORMED
Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) Analysis

METHODOLOGY
FISH analysis was performed using the Vysis LSI SS18 (18q11.2) Dual Color Break Apart Rearrangement Probe (Abbott Molecular). This probe set consists of a SpectrumOrange-labeled probe centromeric to the SS18 gene breakpoint region and a SpectrumGreen-labeled probe telomeric to the breakpoint region. In normal cells, these probes appear as adjacent or fused orange/green signals. Rearrangement of the SS18 gene results in separation of the orange and green signals.

Tissue sections were deparaffinized, pretreated, and hybridized according to manufacturer's protocols. A minimum of 200 interphase nuclei were scored by two independent observers. Positive rearrangement was defined as separation of orange and green signals by more than two signal diameters.

RESULTS
SS18 (18q11.2) Gene Rearrangement: POSITIVE

Quantitative Analysis:
- Total nuclei analyzed: 200
- Nuclei with SS18 rearrangement: 152
- Percentage positive: 76%
- Normal signal pattern: 48 nuclei (24%)

Signal Pattern Distribution:
- 1 fusion, 1 orange, 1 green (typical rearrangement pattern): 148 nuclei
- 2 fusions, 1 orange, 1 green (rearrangement with additional normal copy): 4 nuclei
- 2 fusion signals (normal pattern): 48 nuclei

INTERPRETATION
The FISH analysis demonstrates SS18 gene rearrangement in 76% of analyzed cells, which is diagnostic of synovial sarcoma. This finding confirms the clinical suspicion and is consistent with the characteristic t(X;18) translocation seen in >95% of synovial sarcomas.

The SS18 rearrangement typically results in fusion with one of the SSX family genes (SSX1, SSX2, or rarely SSX4) located on the X chromosome. The specific fusion partner influences tumor behavior, with SS18-SSX1 fusions associated with biphasic histology and SS18-SSX2 fusions more commonly seen in monophasic variants. The resulting fusion oncoprotein acts as an aberrant transcriptional regulator, driving sarcomagenesis through epigenetic mechanisms including antagonism of the BAF chromatin remodeling complex.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
The detection of SS18 rearrangement confirms the diagnosis of synovial sarcoma in this 22-year-old patient. This molecular confirmation has important therapeutic and prognostic implications:

1. Diagnostic certainty: The SS18 rearrangement is pathognomonic for synovial sarcoma, distinguishing it from other spindle cell neoplasms
2. Prognostic information: Young age at diagnosis (<20-25 years) is generally associated with better outcomes
3. Treatment planning: Molecular confirmation supports aggressive multimodal therapy

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Wide surgical resection with negative margins (R0 resection) remains the cornerstone of treatment
2. Adjuvant radiation therapy is strongly recommended given the high risk of local recurrence
3. Consider systemic chemotherapy based on:
   - Tumor size (>5 cm indicates higher risk)
   - Histologic grade
   - Presence of metastatic disease
   - Patient performance status
4. Standard chemotherapy regimens include doxorubicin and ifosfamide
5. Clinical trial enrollment should be considered for novel targeted therapies
6. Long-term surveillance for local recurrence and metastatic disease

REPORTED BY
[redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Director, Molecular Cytogenetics Laboratory

ELECTRONICALLY SIGNED: [redacted date and time]
